findings.title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed/terminated due to wrong isinstance
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the flusher creates processes via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose type is SpawnProcess, but restart and shutdown check isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which on Linux is ForkProcess. A SpawnProcess is not an instance of ForkProcess (both only share BaseProcess), so the check is False in production. As a result process.kill() on hang/crash restart and process.terminate() in join() are never executed. Hung flusher processes leak and the replacement process flushes the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces, Redis contention, and unbounded process accumulation.

findings.title: join() abandons remaining flusher processes on timeout
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py join() sets a deadline, joins next_step with the full timeout, then iterates over flusher processes and breaks out of the loop when the deadline is exceeded. Processes after the break are never waited on nor terminated, and if next_step consumed the whole timeout no flusher is even waited on. Hung or slow flushers are left running after rebalance/shutdown, leaking processes/threads and continuing to flush and produce.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards breaks dashboards
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer on the next line uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}, and segment_size_bytes uses "shard". The pluralization mismatch splits what should be one sharded metric family into different tag keys, breaking aggregation, dashboards, and alerts per shard.

findings.title: Test-mode flusher threads share mutable SpansBuffer with parent
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py when produce_to_pipe is set the code uses threading.Thread with target partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer) and also stores the same shard_buffer object in self.buffers for the parent thread to call record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() in submit(). In production with real processes the child gets a pickled copy, but in tests both threads mutate/read the same SpansBuffer instance concurrently with flush_segments() and its any_shard_at_limit flag without locking. This is a data race that makes tests flaky and unrepresentative of production process isolation.
